name: Lattice QCD: QCD defined and solved non-perturbatively
summary: Wilson's lattice gauge action gives QCD a non-perturbative definition. Monte Carlo sampling of the Euclidean path integral then yields what perturbation theory cannot reach: the string tension and linear confining potential, hadron masses, quark masses and alpha_s.

name: CKM CP violation is too weak for the baryon asymmetry
summary: Sakharov's second condition needs C and CP violation. The CKM phase provides it, but at the electroweak scale its effect is suppressed by the Jarlskog invariant times quark-mass differences to about 1e-20, far below eta_B of about 6e-10, so a new CP-violating source is required.
sources: Sakharov (1967; reprinted 1991). "Violation of CP invariance, C asymmetry, and baryon asymmetry of the universe". *Sov. Phys. Usp.* 34, 392. [doi:10.1070/PU1991v034n05ABEH002497](https://doi.org/10.1070/PU1991v034n05ABEH002497)

name: Peccei-Quinn axion couples through the QCD anomaly
summary: The axion is the pseudo-Goldstone boson of an anomalous U(1)_PQ. The anomaly couples it to G G-tilde exactly like the theta term, so its instanton-generated potential relaxes the effective theta-bar to zero. Its photon coupling is likewise fixed by the electromagnetic anomaly coefficient E/N.

name: QCD is SU(3) Yang-Mills coupled to quarks
summary: QCD is the non-abelian Yang-Mills theory for SU(3) color. The general gauge-theory machinery supplies gluon self-interactions (from the structure constants), Faddeev-Popov ghosts and the sign of the one-loop beta function, as well as the confining phase and the theta vacua.

name: Collinear factorization of amplitudes gives jets
summary: In soft and collinear limits, QCD amplitudes factorize into lower-point amplitudes times universal splitting functions, which makes infrared-safe jet rates computable (Sterman-Weinberg). Spinor-helicity and unitarity methods supply the multi-parton NLO and NNLO matrix elements behind multi-jet predictions.

name: Lattice HVP settles the muon g-2 comparison
summary: Hadronic vacuum polarization limits the SM prediction of a_mu. Lattice QCD (BMW 2020 onward) puts it above the e+e- dispersive value and closer to experiment, and the 2025 Theory Initiative update, which adopts lattice HVP, agrees with the final Fermilab result. The tension within the e+e- data (CMD-3 vs earlier experiments) is still unexplained.
map: a_\mu^{\rm HVP,LO}=\alpha^2\int_0^\infty dt\,K(t)\,G_{\rm em}(t)\ \ (\text{Euclidean vector correlator})
sources: Aoyama et al. (2020). "The anomalous magnetic moment of the muon in the Standard Model". *Phys. Rep.* 887, 1. [arXiv:2006.04822](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.04822)

name: The LHC discovered and now measures the Higgs
summary: ATLAS and CMS discovered the 125 GeV Higgs in 2012, mainly via gluon fusion with H->gamma gamma and ZZ*->4l. The LHC now fits coupling modifiers kappa_i, which agree with the SM at the 5-10% level, and bounds the Higgs self-coupling through HH production.
map: \sigma\cdot{\rm BR}=\frac{\kappa_{\rm prod}^2\kappa_{\rm dec}^2}{\kappa_H^2}(\sigma\cdot{\rm BR})_{\rm SM};\ m_H\approx125\,{\rm GeV}

name: Gauge-coupling unification from RG running
summary: GUTs predict that the three SM gauge couplings meet at one scale. With SM coefficients, one-loop running misses a single meeting point; with MSSM coefficients the couplings meet near 2e16 GeV. That scale sets M_X and so the proton lifetime.

name: B anomalies as tests of lepton-flavor universality
summary: The lepton-universality ratios R_K(*) and R_D(*) in B decays were the flagship flavor anomalies. LHCb's 2022 reanalysis brought R_K(*) back to the SM, while R_D(*) is still about 3 sigma high. The case shows how flavor observables are judged against CKM-based predictions.
map: R_K=\frac{\mathcal B(B\to K\mu\mu)}{\mathcal B(B\to Kee)}\approx1\ ({\rm SM}),\ R_{D^{(*)}}=\frac{\mathcal B(B\to D^{(*)}\tau\nu)}{\mathcal B(B\to D^{(*)}\ell\nu)}

name: keV sterile neutrinos as warm dark matter
summary: A keV-mass gauge-singlet neutrino produced by oscillations (Dodelson-Widrow) or resonantly is a warm dark-matter candidate. X-ray searches for nu_s -> nu gamma and small-scale structure constrain it, and the 3.5 keV line claim is contested and unconfirmed. The eV-scale steriles invoked for the short-baseline anomalies are a separate mass range.

name: Jets are the observable form of QCD partons
summary: Jets trace hard quarks and gluons through showering and hadronization. IR-safe algorithms such as anti-kT make them calculable in perturbative QCD, and jet rates, event shapes and 4-jet angular correlations measure alpha_s and the SU(3) color factors.

name: Electroweak phase transition and baryogenesis
summary: Electroweak baryogenesis needs a strongly first-order transition, so that sphalerons switch off inside expanding bubbles. Lattice studies show the SM transition is a smooth crossover (near 160 GeV) for m_h above about 70 GeV. A 125 GeV Higgs therefore rules out SM electroweak baryogenesis and points to extended scalar sectors that colliders can test.

name: Sphalerons: B+L violation from the electroweak anomaly
summary: Through the SU(2) anomaly, baryon and lepton number change whenever the Chern-Simons number changes ('t Hooft). Tunneling is negligible today, but thermal sphalerons are fast above the electroweak scale. They supply Sakharov's B violation and convert lepton asymmetries into baryons while conserving B-L.
map: \partial_\mu j_B^\mu=\partial_\mu j_L^\mu=\frac{N_f}{32\pi^2}\left(g^2W\tilde W-g'^2B\tilde B\right),\ \Delta B=\Delta L=N_f\Delta N_{CS}

name: Leptogenesis and Majorana neutrino mass
summary: In thermal leptogenesis, the heavy Majorana neutrinos of the seesaw decay CP-asymmetrically and sphalerons convert the resulting lepton asymmetry into baryons. Seeing neutrinoless double-beta decay would establish the lepton-number violation and Majorana nature leptogenesis needs, but would not fix its high-scale CP phases.

name: Asymptotic freedom and dimensional transmutation
summary: The one-loop beta function of SU(3) with six flavors is negative, so alpha_s falls logarithmically at high Q (Gross-Wilczek and Politzer, 1973). The classically scale-free theory also generates the hadronic scale Lambda_QCD, a few hundred MeV, from a dimensionless coupling.

name: Axial anomaly: eta' mass and pi0 -> gamma gamma
summary: QCD has no ninth Goldstone boson because the anomaly and instantons break U(1)_A ('t Hooft). The Witten-Veneziano relation ties the eta' mass to the topological susceptibility, and the pi0 -> gamma gamma rate, fixed by the anomaly coefficient, confirms N_c = 3.

name: Chiral perturbation theory: EFT of QCD's Goldstones
summary: Spontaneous breaking of SU(3)_L x SU(3)_R to SU(3)_V makes the pions, kaons and eta pseudo-Goldstone bosons. Chiral perturbation theory (Weinberg, Gasser-Leutwyler) is the EFT that expands in p/Lambda_chi, with Lambda_chi of about 4 pi f_pi, roughly 1 GeV. Its leading term gives the GMOR relation.
map: \mathcal L_2=\frac{f^2}{4}{\rm Tr}(\partial_\mu U\partial^\mu U^\dagger)+\frac{f^2B}{2}{\rm Tr}(MU^\dagger+UM^\dagger)\Rightarrow m_\pi^2=B(m_u+m_d)

name: Hadron spectrum and exotics from lattice QCD
summary: Lattice QCD reproduces the light hadron spectrum at the percent level (BMW 2008) and, with QED added, the neutron-proton mass splitting. Resonances and exotic candidates (X(3872), T_cc, hybrids) are studied by mapping finite-volume energy levels to scattering amplitudes with the Lüscher method.

name: Soft-collinear EFT resums jet and event-shape logs
summary: SCET separates hard, collinear and soft modes with power counting lambda ~ p_T/Q and proves factorization theorems for jet observables. The RG evolution of each factor resums Sudakov double logarithms. It is used for thrust-based alpha_s fits, jet vetoes and jet mass.

name: Parton showers and string hadronization model QCD
summary: Parton showers implement DGLAP evolution as a Markov chain with Sudakov no-emission probabilities. Hadronization uses either the Lund string, a linear confining flux tube that breaks by Schwinger-like q-qbar tunneling, or cluster models built on preconfinement.
breaks: Shower kernels follow from QCD factorization, but hadronization models are phenomenological, with parameters tuned to data rather than derived from QCD.

name: Normalizing flows for lattice gauge-field sampling
summary: Generative models from HEP machine learning, notably gauge-equivariant normalizing flows (Albergo, Kanwar, Shanahan and collaborators), are trained to sample lattice field configurations directly. The aim is to beat critical slowing down and topological freezing near the continuum limit. The same flow technology also drives phase-space sampling in event generators.
breaks: Flows are not yet competitive with HMC at physical QCD volumes, and their training cost grows steeply with lattice volume.

name: Hierarchy problem: the unprotected Higgs mass
summary: The Higgs mass term is the SM's only relevant operator and no symmetry protects it, so heavy thresholds feed into m_H^2. Large and warped extra dimensions, compositeness and SUSY are the proposed cures, and LHC null results sharpen the puzzle into the little hierarchy problem.
breaks: In dimensional regularization no Lambda^2 appears; the physical issue is sensitivity to the masses of heavy new particles, and naturalness is a criterion, not a law.

name: SUSY Higgs mass bound and the 125 GeV Higgs
summary: Boson-fermion loop cancellation removes the quadratic sensitivity of m_H^2, and the MSSM predicts a light Higgs with m_h <= m_Z |cos 2beta| at tree level. Reaching 125 GeV needs large stop loop corrections, from multi-TeV stops or maximal mixing, which is in tension with naturalness.

name: sin^2 theta_W = 3/8 at the unification scale
summary: Embedding SU(3)xSU(2)xU(1) in SU(5) fixes the hypercharge normalization, g_1 = sqrt(5/3) g', so sin^2 theta_W = 3/8 at the unification scale. Running down to m_Z gives about 0.21 in the SM and close to the measured 0.2312 in the MSSM. The same embedding explains charge quantization (Q_d = Q_e/3).

name: W mass: precision electroweak test and the CDF outlier
summary: The W mass follows from G_F, alpha and m_Z plus loop corrections Delta r that depend on the top and Higgs masses, which makes it a sharp new-physics probe (through the oblique T parameter). CDF's 2022 value sits about 7 sigma above the SM, but ATLAS (2024) and CMS (2024) agree with the SM, so CDF is treated as an unresolved outlier.

name: Fermi theory as the EFT of W exchange; SMEFT
summary: Fermi's four-fermion contact interaction is the low-energy limit of W exchange. It violates unitarity below about 1 TeV, which pointed to the weak scale. It is the template for SMEFT, where dimension-6 operators suppressed by Lambda^2 parametrize heavy new physics in electroweak and Higgs data.

name: Gauge-anomaly cancellation fixes SM charges
summary: SU(3)xSU(2)xU(1) is consistent only because gauge and mixed gauge-gravitational anomalies cancel within each generation, quarks against leptons. This requires N_c = 3 and the observed hypercharges, and it implies charge quantization. Witten's global SU(2) anomaly further requires an even number of doublets.

name: Running Higgs quartic: electroweak vacuum metastability
summary: With m_h = 125 GeV and m_t of about 172.5 GeV, NNLO running drives the Higgs quartic lambda negative near 1e10-1e11 GeV. The electroweak vacuum is therefore metastable, with a lifetime far beyond the age of the universe. The conclusion depends sensitively on m_t and alpha_s.

name: Weinberg operator: neutrino mass at dimension 5 in SMEFT
summary: Weinberg's (LH)(LH)/Lambda is the only dimension-5 operator built from SM fields, and it gives Majorana neutrino masses m_nu ~ v^2/Lambda. A mass near 0.05 eV then points to Lambda of 1e14-1e15 GeV. Seesaw types I-III are its tree-level UV completions, and neutrinoless double-beta decay tests its Delta L = 2.
map: \frac{c}{\Lambda}(\bar L^c\tilde H^*)(\tilde H^\dagger L)\ \to\ m_\nu\sim\frac{c\,v^2}{\Lambda},\ \text{type I: }\frac{c}{\Lambda}=\frac{y^2}{M_R}

name: MSW effect from charged-current forward scattering
summary: Coherent forward scattering of nu_e on electrons through W exchange adds a potential sqrt2 G_F n_e that changes the effective mixing; the flavor-universal Z-exchange term cancels for active neutrinos. The adiabatic MSW resonance explains the energy dependence of solar nu_e survival (SNO, Borexino) and gives long-baseline experiments sensitivity to the mass ordering.

name: PMNS and CKM: the same unitary mixing structure
summary: PMNS and CKM are both 3x3 unitary matrices that arise because mass and weak-interaction bases are misaligned. They share the parametrization (three angles and one Dirac phase, plus two Majorana phases for PMNS) and the Jarlskog invariant that controls CP violation. T2K, NOvA, DUNE and Hyper-K measure leptonic CP violation as the difference between nu_mu->nu_e and the antineutrino channel.
breaks: CKM angles are small and hierarchical while PMNS angles are large. Neutrino masses may be Majorana (seesaw) rather than Yukawa. Matter effects mimic a CP asymmetry in long-baseline data.

name: Strong CP problem and axion mass from QCD topology
summary: QCD allows a CP-violating theta-bar = theta + arg det M_q, and the neutron EDM bound forces |theta-bar| below about 1e-10: the strong CP problem the axion solves. The axion mass is set by QCD's topological susceptibility, m_a^2 f_a^2 = chi_top, and lattice results for chi_top(T) fix the axion relic abundance from misalignment.
map: \bar\theta=\theta+\arg\det M_q\lesssim10^{-10};\ m_a^2f_a^2=\chi_{\rm top},\ m_a\approx5.7\,\mu{\rm eV}\left(\frac{10^{12}\,{\rm GeV}}{f_a}\right)

name: Warped extra dimension dual to a composite-Higgs CFT
summary: By the AdS/CFT dictionary, a Randall-Sundrum slice of AdS5 with an IR brane is dual to a strongly coupled, nearly conformal 4D theory that confines at the TeV scale. KK modes map to composite resonances, the IR-brane Higgs to a composite Higgs, and the warp factor to the RG scale (Arkani-Hamed-Porrati-Randall 2001).
map: z\leftrightarrow1/\mu,\ \text{IR brane}\leftrightarrow\Lambda_{\rm comp}\sim{\rm TeV},\ m_{\rm KK}\leftrightarrow m_\rho,\ \Delta=2+\sqrt{4+m^2L^2}
breaks: The duality is derived only for large-N theories with string duals such as N=4 SYM. The CFT dual to a phenomenological RS model is not known explicitly, so the map is a heuristic dictionary.

name: QED to five loops in the lepton g-2
summary: The Schwinger term alpha/2pi began the precision testing of perturbative QFT. The QED part of the lepton anomalous moment is now known to tenth order (12,672 diagrams; Aoyama, Kinoshita, Nio). The electron g-2 therefore measures alpha at the sub-ppb level, while the muon g-2 uncertainty is dominated by non-perturbative hadronic loops.
sources: Aoyama et al. (2020). "The anomalous magnetic moment of the muon in the Standard Model". *Phys. Rep.* 887, 1. [arXiv:2006.04822](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.04822)

name: Weak effective Hamiltonian and Wilson coefficients
summary: Flavor-changing decays are computed with a weak effective Hamiltonian obtained by integrating out W, Z and top. The operator product expansion separates short-distance Wilson coefficients, run from m_W to m_b with anomalous dimensions, from long-distance hadronic matrix elements. New physics shows up as shifts such as C_9 and C_10 in b -> s l l.

name: Lattice decay constants and form factors fix CKM
summary: Extracting CKM elements needs hadronic inputs that only lattice QCD supplies at percent precision: decay constants (f_K/f_pi, f_B), the kaon bag parameter B_K for epsilon_K, and B->D* and B->pi form factors for |V_cb| and |V_ub|. FLAG averages feed the unitarity-triangle fits, and the first-row unitarity deficit depends on these inputs.
